clue.text: Polish ruse uncovered in instructions

parts.note: to polish is to rub

indicators.note: uncovered means the word's outer letters, its covers, are stripped away

parts.note: a ruse is a trick

explanation.surface: A rule sheet warns that a Polish scam is hidden in the instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: Polish looks like the nationality, but it is the verb meaning to shine.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubric is a heading or set of directions, as on an exam paper telling candidates what to do.

clue.text: One stops backing socially unacceptable marriage

indicators.note: the one letter stops up, or plugs, the gap in the middle of the other word
backing means the word for socially unacceptable is read from its back

parts.note: NON-U is the British label for language or manners not used by the upper class
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone stops supporting a match that society frowns upon.
explanation.walkthrough: NON-U is a mid-century British term for what the upper classes regard as vulgar, the opposite of U.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a joining of two people in wedlock, a common formal synonym for marriage.

clue.text: Knocking sound thrice at bottom of door, moving to the top

indicators.note: the piece from the door's bottom goes up to sit at the head of the entry
in a down entry the bottom of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word door
the word at written three times over

explanation.surface: Instructions for a rhythm: knock three times low on the door, then move up.
explanation.definitionFit: Rat-a-tat imitates the sound of repeated rapping on a door, an onomatopoeic word for knocking.

clue.text: Former deputy PM caught at last concealing housing support

indicators.note: the two letters together house, or enclose, the support
at last means only the final letter of the following word is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word concealing
a leg is something that holds up a table or chair

explanation.surface: An ex-politician is caught at last, hiding something about property subsidies.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught. Nick Clegg was the UK Deputy Prime Minister from 2010 to 2015, in the coalition government.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Clegg led the Liberal Democrats and served as Britain's deputy prime minister under David Cameron.

clue.text: Determined, cunning individual nearly swore

indicators.note: nearly means the word stops just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a fox is proverbially sly, so a cunning person is called a fox
to cuss is to swear

explanation.surface: A resolute schemer almost let loose a curse.
explanation.definitionFit: Being focussed means concentrating single-mindedly on a goal, much like being resolute or set on something.

clue.text: Character of Marlowe in uniform punching dissolute American

indicators.note: the letter punches its way into the middle of the other word

parts.note: fast in the old sense of living a wild, pleasure-seeking life
U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A stage figure in a uniform throws a punch at a debauched American.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Faustus is Christopher Marlowe's play about the scholar who sells his soul to the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Faustus is the title figure of Marlowe's Elizabethan tragedy, a protagonist in that play.

clue.text: Theatre critic, one producing disengaged bollocks?

definitions.note: a gelder produces testicles that are no longer engaged, i.e. detached

parts.note: the cast is the company of actors in a theatre production
a critic rates performances, so is a rater

explanation.surface: A reviewer is accused of writing lazy, half-hearted nonsense about a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Bollocks is British slang for nonsense and also for testicles; the definition plays on the anatomical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrater removes the testicles of an animal, leaving them detached from the body.

clue.text: Old boy abandoning watchful attendant

indicators.note: the old boy abandons the word, leaving its remaining letters

parts.note: an observant person is watchful
OB is the standard short form for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A former pupil leaves behind a watchful caretaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A servant waits on someone, as an attendant does; both are people employed to serve.

clue.text: Empathise, taking top off to provide joy

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, here removed

parts.note: to relate to someone is to empathise with them

explanation.surface: Showing sympathy, minus the pretence, makes people happy.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate someone is to fill them with happiness, to make them delighted.

clue.text: Perhaps tip-off impacted new charges

indicators.note: charges in the sense of loads up, so the word takes the letter into itself

parts.note: something that impacted hit

explanation.surface: An informant's tip led to fresh criminal charges.
explanation.walkthrough: Perhaps signals that a tip-off is only one kind of hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip-off is a discreet warning or piece of advance information, one kind of clue or suggestion.

clue.text: Is Queen Rat travelling on horseback?

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters are on the move, rearranging themselves

parts.note: the three words supply exactly the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about whether a rodent royal is riding.
explanation.definitionFit: Equestrian describes anything relating to horse riding, such as a statue of a mounted rider.

clue.text: Popular man occupying dump next to a hill is prime mover

parts.note: something popular is in
Stig of the Dump is a British children's novel about a caveman living in a chalk pit
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A well-liked tramp living beside a hillside tip turns out to be the ringleader.
explanation.walkthrough: Stig of the Dump, by Clive King, is a staple of British childhoods; a tor is a craggy hilltop in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An instigator is the person who starts or provokes something, its originating force.

clue.text: Region in Near East

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the following words

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of Near and start of East

explanation.surface: A geographical label placing a region in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a tract or zone of land, the same idea as a region.

clue.text: Expenses covering ten swimming competitions

indicators.note: the outer word covers, or wraps around, the scrambled number

parts.note: expenses are costs

indicators.note: swimming letters are moving about, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: the number word itself supplies the three letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The bill for ten swimming events comes to quite a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Contests are events in which people compete against one another, matches or tournaments.

clue.text: Joke about Spain

definitions.note: as in 'have you heard the one about...'

parts.note: on means concerning, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A gag concerning Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España).
explanation.definitionFit: A one is colloquially a joke or story, as in a comedian asking if you have heard the one about the vicar.

clue.text: Worry about pal dancing without over-the-shoulder support

indicators.note: the worry goes about, encircling the jumbled friend

parts.note: stress is worry or anxiety

indicators.note: the friend's letters are dancing, moving into a new order

parts.note: the word pal itself supplies the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone frets about a friend dancing in a dress with no straps.
explanation.definitionFit: A strapless garment, typically a dress or bra, has no straps passing over the shoulders to hold it up.

clue.text: Painter from India embraced by intellectual giant

indicators.note: the letter is hugged inside the other word

parts.note: a titan is a person of great stature, here in learning
I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An artist from India is hugged by a towering thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: India looks like where the painter comes from, but it is just a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was the great Venetian Renaissance artist, so he is an example of a painter.

clue.text: Periodically laugh at Turkish commander

indicators.note: periodically means taking letters at regular intervals, every other one

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone now and then mocks an Ottoman officer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga (or agha) was a military officer or chief in the Ottoman Empire, a title of command.

clue.text: Politician: "Learn to ignore religious classes"

indicators.note: the letters for religious classes are ignored, left out

parts.note: to learn something is to commit it to memory, to remember it
RE is religious education, a British school subject

explanation.surface: A politician advises skipping religion lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for religious education, the British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A Member of Parliament is called a member, so the word stands for an elected politician.

clue.text: Modest party with coke, perhaps, but ecstasy discarded

parts.note: a bash is a party

indicators.note: the drug is thrown away from the word

parts.note: coke here is the coal-derived fuel, not the drug or drink
E is the street name for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A shy partygoer had cocaine but threw away the ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Coke looks like the drug, given the party and ecstasy, but it is the solid fuel made from coal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bashful means being shy and self-effacing, much like being modest.

clue.text: German in docking area left on the edge

indicators.note: the German letter is placed in the docking area and its neighbour

parts.note: a marina is a harbour for yachts and small boats

explanation.surface: A German in a harbour wanders off to its fringe.
explanation.definitionFit: Marginal means lying at the margin or border, so at the edge of something.

clue.text: Like sheep meat or dog but not llama, at first

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: not means the following letter is removed

parts.note: but in the sense of only, as in 'but a child'

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is used

parts.note: the first letter of llama

explanation.surface: A culinary query: does this taste of mutton, dog, or anything but llama?
explanation.walkthrough: But looks like a conjunction joining the list, but it stands for only.
explanation.definitionFit: Muttony describes a flavour or texture resembling mutton, which is the flesh of a mature sheep.

clue.text: Practical knowledge from one changed things

indicators.note: the letters of the word are changed, put into a new order

parts.note: the word things itself supplies the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone gains wisdom by finding that one thing is different.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is a deep understanding of how something actually works, useful knowledge gained by perception.

clue.text: British leaving fundamental ingredient unaltered

indicators.note: the British letter leaves the word, which goes on without it

parts.note: the basis of something is its fundamental component

explanation.surface: A British cook leaves the key ingredient exactly as it was.
explanation.definitionFit: Sold as is means sold in its current condition, without any changes being made.

clue.text: Mark acted as a substitute? Time to get promoted

indicators.note: time is T, and promoted in a down clue means that letter moves up, ahead of the A before it

parts.note: to sit in is to act as a substitute for someone, so sat in

explanation.surface: A cover teacher marks work, and a hint that it is time for promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: SAT IN is the phrase; 'Time to get promoted' moves its T up one place, so SATIN becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain is a blot or discoloured spot, so it is a mark left on something.

clue.text: Maybe Humphries' alter ego beginning to grasp Gilbert and Sullivan's speciality

parts.note: Sir Les Patterson, the boorish Australian cultural attache, was one of Barry Humphries' comic characters

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of grasp

explanation.surface: A comic persona starts to understand the light-opera duo's trademark.
explanation.walkthrough: Barry Humphries is best known as Dame Edna Everage, so Maybe is needed: Les Patterson was his other famous creation.
explanation.definitionFit: A patter song is a fast comic song with tongue-twisting lyrics, a hallmark of Gilbert and Sullivan's operettas.

clue.text: Arrive in burlesque performance when son thrown out

indicators.note: the son is thrown out of the word, leaving the rest

parts.note: a send-up is a parody, a mocking imitation

explanation.surface: A spoof show turns up after a son is ejected.
explanation.definitionFit: To end up somewhere is to finish there, to reach or get to a place eventually.

clue.text: Stand up, extremely sensitive and tender

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to stand for election is to run

indicators.note: extremely means only the outer letters, the extremes, are used

parts.note: the first and last letters of sensitive

explanation.surface: Someone rises, very sensitive and sore.
explanation.walkthrough: Tender looks like an adjective, sore, but it is the verb meaning to care for.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a patient is to look after them, to tend or care for them.

clue.text: Sentient computer following subordinate for a moment

parts.note: HAL 9000 is the thinking computer in the film 2001: A Space Odyssey
a second is a deputy or assistant, one ranked below

explanation.surface: A thinking machine trails behind an underling, for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Following looks like it orders the pieces, but it is just the letter F.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-second is a tiny span of time, an instant or brief moment.

clue.text: It's bloody good source of metal

definitions.note: the definition describes a substance, blood shed in violence

parts.note: ore is rock from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a metal ore is really excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloody looks like a British intensifier, as in bloody good, but it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gore is blood that has been shed, especially in quantity from a wound.

clue.text: Director mostly agreed to go round Welsh island

indicators.note: mostly means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Ang Lee, the Taiwanese film director of Brokeback Mountain and Life of Pi

indicators.note: going round means the word turns about, read backwards

parts.note: yes is the word of agreement

explanation.surface: A film-maker nearly consents to circle a Welsh island.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglesey is the large island off the north-west coast of Wales, across the Menai Strait.

clue.text: Spirit of youngster on river

indicators.note: in an across entry, one piece on another means it comes after it

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
a teen is a teenager

explanation.surface: A young person floats down a river, seemingly in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Poteen is Irish moonshine, illicitly distilled from potatoes or grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Poteen is a strong Irish alcoholic drink, a type of distilled liquor.
